transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood CSM), Laura Mendes (Mapleway Procurement), Evan Cho (Mapleway InfoSec), Samir Patel (Mapleway MLOps), Tasha Reid (Mapleway Finance)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah appreciate you all making time. I'm Jordan, I'll lead commercial for this intake. Quick round-robin?
[00:18] Laura: Laura here, procurement, finalizing who signs the MSA. We're on a tight cadence, FY end approvals in two weeks.
[00:26] Evan: Evan, InfoSec — we'll focus on KMS, SSO, and audit logs.
[00:32] Samir: Samir, MLOps — we'll drive the pilot and run the workloads.
[00:36] Tasha: Tasha, finance — looking at pricing pathways and escrow.
[00:40] Priya: Priya from Redwood SE, hi all, I'll run the technical checks and the benchmark.
[00:45] Jordan: Cool. Agenda is quick: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations (latency and uptime), KMS and keying, pricing options — hosted vs dedicated — and pilot acceptance criteria.

[02:02] Jordan: Laura you mentioned two-week approvals, can you confirm decision makers and any blockers?
[02:12] Laura: Yep, procurement plus fin ops. The last blocker was egress fees. We need pricing clear on egress and retained tokens, also DPA clauses for EU data residency.
[02:24] Jordan: Understood. We have a couple of routes: hosted API with per-token billing and region pinning, or Redwood Dedicated with committed capacity and predictable throughput.
[02:36] Tasha: What's the delta on unit price for Dedicated? ballpark percent.
[02:40] Jordan: For sustained throughput, Dedicated reduces unit cost roughly 35-45% depending on commit. We'll send modeled examples.

[03:10] Samir: On the technical side, we need tail-latency SLOs. Our users need sub-300ms 95th for short prompts. Can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[03:22] Priya: Uh, so for short prompts — yeah — we usually hit ~120-180ms p95 in us-west region for the curated small-latency models. For heavier models and long context, we recommend Dedicated or latency-tiered routing. There was a note in our perf doc about KV cache priming for chat workloads — that helps.
[03:44] Evan: When you say 'curated small-latency models' is that like Redwood's verified catalog or a different name?
[03:50] Priya: It's the curated catalog, sometimes in transcripts it shows as 'Redwood Verif' — um the proper name is Redwood-verified performance profiles.

[04:10] Laura: On MSA: we have two proposed exceptions: 1) data deletion timing for logs (we want 90 days), 2) liability cap for security incidents. Can you speak to Redwood's standard?
[04:24] Jordan: Standard MSA has 180-day logs retention for analytics but can scope logs differently by contract — DPA and SLAs can pin retention. Liability cap — standard is 1x annualized fees but we can negotiate for enterprise. We'll flag those in the redline.
[04:40] Tasha: Are there escrow or clawback options? We have some vendors that require code escrow.
[04:46] Jordan: We don't generally provide code escrow for hosted, but for Dedicated or Private deployment we can discuss escrow or more robust exit assistance. We'll put options in the playbook.

[05:30] Evan: KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys via HSM in cloud KMS? We need to ensure keys never leave our control.
[05:40] Priya: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and there's an HSM-backed path. For Private on-prem installs, you control the HSM. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption where Redwood never sees the plaintext key material.
[05:56] Samir: Is there an option for bring-your-own-HSM for Dedicated?
[06:00] Priya: For Dedicated, yes, bring-your-own-keying is supported; we'll confirm the exact workflow (KMIP/Cloud-HSM integration). I'll capture the config steps.

[06:30] Laura: For DPA we need data residency — EU data must stay in EU AZ. Are regional controls on by default?
[06:38] Jordan: You can pin region on hosted for model endpoints; Dedicated pools can be created in chosen region. There is a small premium for regional isolation. We'll include region pinning in the pricing model.

[07:10] Samir: On pilot scope — we want to run our Q&A microservice and a reranking job. Acceptance criteria: throughput 200 qps sustained for 30 minutes, p95 < 300ms, and embedding similarity within our eval threshold. Who signs off?
[07:26] Jordan: Usually engineering confirms perf, procurement signs on commercial. For acceptance, we should capture sign-off owners: Samir for tech, Laura for procurement, Tasha for finance.

[08:00] Priya: I'll propose an evaluation plan: three model variants (small, med-quant, quantized large) across both hosted and dedicated setups. I can run a 1-day bench and produce a CSV with latency percentiles and cost per million tokens.
[08:18] Samir: That works. We need the CSV to include GPU hours, token counts, and KV cache hit ratio.

[09:05] Evan: About audit logs — do you provide token-level tracing and per-request audit trails for compliance?
[09:13] Marcus: Marcus chiming — Redwood Console gives request traces and token-level cost breakdown, plus append-only audit logs we can pipe to customer SIEM via connectors. For high-security customers we support longer retention and SIEM forwarding.
[09:28] Evan: Great. Is the SIEM integration pull or push?
[09:32] Marcus: Push via secure syslog/HTTPS endpoint or S3 export, depending on your infra.

[10:00] Laura: Regarding SLA, our legal team wants explicit latency SLOs and credits for breach. Most vendors give uptime credits for downtime but not latency. Can you support latency SLOs?
[10:12] Jordan: We can define latency SLOs for specific routes/models that are pinned to Dedicated or latency-tiered hosted endpoints. Credits for latency misses are negotiable but need to be scoped (e.g., if measured p95 over monthly window exceeds threshold).
[10:28] Laura: We prefer a clear measurement method — agree on telemetry source and sample windows.
[10:34] Priya: We can instrument with the same telemetry as Console and provide the measurement dashboard. I'd propose rolling 30-day windows and p95 measured at model-route level.

[11:05] Tasha: For pricing approvals — procurement wants a clean comparitive table: hosted list price, dedicated committed pricing, and uplift for region pinning/kms.
[11:15] Jordan: We'll share a pricing matrix and example cost model spreadsheets; also include egress estimates and retention costs.

[12:00] Samir: A couple of technical edges: 1) can Redwood do model fallbacks if a heavy model isn't available? 2) Any pre-warm or steady-state cache guidance?
[12:12] Priya: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants, and prefix/KV caching helps reduce cold-starts. For pre-warm, Dedicated clusters can reserve GPU pools and primed KV caches.

[12:45] Evan: A security nit: will logs ever contain PII? If so, how is masking handled?
[12:52] Priya: By default logs can include request metadata but we have options to redacted PII and transform hooks. You can also configure client-side masking or tokenization prior to sending.

[13:20] Laura: On the DPA — do you accept sub-processor lists and will Redwood provide a list upfront?
[13:27] Jordan: Yes, Redwood will provide a subprocessor list and update cadence. We'll include that in the DPA exhibit.

[14:00] (crosstalk) Speaker 1: sorry can I just ask — do you support SAML 2.0 for SSO?
[14:06] Marcus: Yes, SAML2.0 and OIDC both supported, SSO via SAML is enterprise-ready with SCIM for provisioning.

[15:00] Samir: For the benchmark — we will provide a representational dataset of 10k queries and a reranking set. Any data handling concerns sharing that?
[15:12] Evan: we'll label that as vendor eval data, but we need it redacted for customer PII; we'll coordinate.
[15:18] Priya: Perfect — for bench we prefer a sanitized sample; we can also run synthetic traffic if needed.

[16:00] Laura: On MSA timelines: procurement needs a redline back within 5 business days to meet our internal gates. Is that feasible?
[16:08] Jordan: We can aim for 5 business days for first-pass redline. If legal exceptions are complex it may take longer, but we'll prioritize.

[16:40] Tasha: Billing — how are credits and refunds handled? Monthly invoice?
[16:46] Jordan: Monthly invoices with line items per route/model. Credits for SLA breaches applied as invoice credit in the following billing cycle. We can arrange escrow or advanced payment terms for Dedicated commitments.

[17:30] Evan: Can we get an architecture sketch for Private deployment? We might consider a hybrid — control plane in Redwood but data plane in our VPC.
[17:40] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed data plane—control plane remains in our (Redwood) management plane optionally. We'll send an architecture diagram.

[18:10] Samir: A question about inference reproducibility: do you pin model versions so that outputs don't drift during the pilot?
[18:16] Priya: Absolutely — you can pin model versions and Redwood supports model rollouts and versioning. Rollback policies are built into the console.

[19:00] Laura: Any blockers around export controls or data residency for the EU?
[19:07] Jordan: No immediate blockers, but we'll capture export-control obligations in the DPA. For EU residency, we'll pin regions and include contractual language.

[19:40] Marcus: I'll summarize the technical deliverables: architecture diagram, KMS integration steps, bench CSV, and the Console demo recording.

[20:10] Jordan: And commercial deliverables: initial redline MSA/DPA, pricing matrix, and a sample SLA clause for latency credits.

[21:00] Laura: For sign-off, procurement needs one consolidated doc with redlines and a cover note.
[21:06] Jordan: We'll do that.

[22:00] (pause)
[22:15] Samir: One more nit on model quantization — will Redwood provide guidance if we use int8 or int4 variants — impact on quality?
[22:24] Priya: We'll include a quantization recommendation per workload; Redwood Optimize has a runbook for quantization vs quality tradeoffs. We'll run the recommended evals.

[23:00] Tasha: How soon can we get pricing scenarios? We need those to prep the finance approval.
[23:08] Jordan: We'll send a first-pass pricing matrix within two business days, then updated after the bench numbers.

[24:00] Evan: Any compliance certs we should be aware of? SOC2 Type II is listed right?
[24:06] Marcus: Yes SOC2 Type II; we can provide the attestation and any ISO reports on request.

[25:30] Laura: Ok — mapping of people: Samir tech sign-off, Laura procurement sign-off, Tasha finance sign-off.

[26:00] Jordan: Great. Quick callouts on risks: egress fees and retention costs could drive overages—we'll highlight scenario A/B/C in the cost model.

[27:10] Samir: Will the bench simulate KV cache hit patterns? That's important for our chat flow.
[27:16] Priya: Yes, I'll include a KV cache simulation and report hit ratio.

[28:00] (small interruption) Speaker 1: I might be on mute — sorry — agreement on timeline?
[28:07] Laura: Yes 5 biz days redline, bench by 2026-01-20, pricing matrix within 2 biz days.

[29:00] Jordan: Anything else?
[29:05] Evan: On the DPA, we'd like a clause for incident notification windows — 24-hour initial and 72-hour full report. Is that acceptable?
[29:14] Jordan: We'll accept 24-hour initial notification for security incidents; full investigative report timeline we can negotiate — we'll propose 72 hours as a target.

[30:00] Tasha: For Dedicated entitlements — can we have a trial month before commit?
[30:08] Jordan: We can do a short pilot with credit applied toward the commit if you convert within 30 days. Will document in the commercial summary.

[31:00] Samir: Any limitations on private deployment for some model architectures?
[31:06] Priya: Certain bleeding-edge models require specific driver/kernel stacks; our private package includes supported stacks list. We'll share compatibility matrix.

[32:00] Laura: Ok let's record next steps again for clarity.
[32:05] Jordan: Sure. Jordan: Redwood will share the redline (Jordan), Priya will run bench and share CSV (Priya), Marcus will send console demo and SOC2 (Marcus). Mapleway (Samir/Evan/Laura) will provide sanitized sample and data classification.

[33:00] Laura: I'll aim to route the redline through legal the same day we get it.

[34:00] Jordan: Anything blocking the pricing approval then?
[34:05] Tasha: Finance needs the matrix to compare cloud spend and committed pricing — once received we'll review.

[35:00] (brief talk about calendar invites)

[37:00] Jordan: Ok final recap: deliverables, owners and dates — we've captured those. Anything else to add?
[37:10] Samir: No, sounds good.
[37:15] Evan: No.
[37:18] Laura: None.

[38:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll push the redline by 2026-01-19 and bench by 2026-01-20. Expect a follow-up invite for a demo and bench-readout next week.

[38:30] (end)

Transcript notes: auto-generated transcription. Some product names and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., 'Redwood Verif' instead of Redwood-verified). Occasional speaker mis-attribution labeled as 'Speaker 1'.
